A person asks for a video on a topic. That request starts the recipe.
Clé reads a README or group totals. Only public text or group totals, never patient data, because Clé may not see patient data.
Clé splits the topic into chapters, one idea each.
Clé writes spoken beats and a Python drawing function per chapter. Each picture moment ties to a beat, with a red ring and short label.
A harness runs the code and renders one frame per beat. Crashes send errors back to Clé.
Clé lists overlaps and cut-off text. A fact check compares narration with source. Complaints go back, at most four rounds.
Kokoro makes the voice on the workstation CPU. In Clé's films, matplotlib draws frames, twenty four per second. ffmpeg joins picture and sound.

A person watches and decides. The model does not decide it is right. Other uses are only proposals: explaining a segmentation result, a tutorial with invented data, a status report from logs, or onboarding from a README. Patient images and tables must not go to Clé, so those chapters need the local model.
